claims.text: A combined DSC, in-situ neutron-imaging, and CALPHAD approach can determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, melting-associated volume change, and other liquid thermodynamic properties across homogeneous high-entropy alloys.
The combined approach is high-throughput and efficient.
An inert atmosphere avoids oxidation during thermal measurements.
Uniform starting microstructures minimize phase-separation effects during measurement.
High configurational entropy is intrinsic to the targeted high-entropy alloys.
High configurational entropy ensures atomic-scale homogeneity in the liquid state.
Liquid-state atomic homogeneity facilitates reproducible thermal transitions and reproducible volume changes at melting.
DSC precisely identifies the endothermic peak associated with melting.
In-situ neutron imaging can capture melting and liquid-state evolution of high-entropy alloys in real time.
Neutron imaging can directly quantify real-time volumetric changes during fusion.
CALPHAD can refine latent-heat and volume-expansion measurements into quantitative fusion and liquid-phase thermodynamic parameters.
Thermodynamics-based computational models can reproduce qualitative and quantitative features of temperature- and composition-dependent phase evolution in high-entropy alloys.
Fusion temperatures and latent heats can be measured within 5–10% error relative to benchmarks from simpler alloys.
The integrated method will yield reliable composition-dependent thermodynamic data across a broad range of high-entropy-alloy systems.
Traditional DSC studies of simpler alloys generally use slower heating rates and separate post-melting thermodynamic modeling.
Some high-entropy-alloy systems exhibit liquid-phase immiscibility.
Liquid-phase immiscibility or segregation increases uncertainty in the proposed fusion-property measurements.
Extreme phase competition or subtle ordering effects increase measurement uncertainty by altering liquid-state behavior.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator says high configurational entropy ensures liquid-state homogeneity, whereas the boundary explicitly recognizes high-entropy-alloy systems with liquid-phase immiscibility or segregation.
